summary: Legacy CHOP for sequencing a DAT-listed set of CHOPs with blend/add scopes, queueing, trigger, and reset controls.
key_concepts: Sequencer CHOP is a legacy timed-sequencing operator that has been replaced by Timer CHOP.
Current official docs say Sequencer CHOP has been removed for creation but still works in existing files.
DAT List points to a table of CHOP paths that the legacy sequencer will transition through.
Blend Scope and Add Scope decide which channels blend, add, or jump during transitions.
Queue, Trigger, Reset, and Reset Pulse control pausing, immediate transition, and reset-to-default behavior.
Use this card primarily for diagnosing or migrating legacy networks; new timed processes should use Timer CHOP and official OP Snippets.

common_gotchas: Official docs say Timer CHOP replaces Sequencer CHOP.
Sequencer CHOP has been removed for new creation in current builds, though it may still work in existing files.
Generated plans should prefer Timer CHOP and Operator Snippets examples for timed processes.
Only use this card for legacy project diagnosis or migration planning.
If a legacy file still contains Sequencer CHOP, DAT List paths must resolve to the sequenced CHOPs.
Blend Scope and Add Scope decide transition behavior per channel, so broad scopes can change animation unexpectedly.
build_relevance: legacy timed sequencing; prefer Timer CHOP
